paragraphs.title: Jeremiah's Complaint and God's Response about the Wicked

answers: When the temple will be rebuilt
easy.explanation: Jeremiah asks, “Wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper?”
easy.q: What does Jeremiah ask about the wicked?

answers: As people who have lost their possessions
easy.explanation: They are described as planted, taking root, growing, and bringing forth fruit.
easy.q: How are the wicked described in verse 2?

answers: His brethren and the house of his father
easy.explanation: The Lord says that even Jeremiah's brethren and his father's house have dealt treacherously with him.
easy.q: Whom does the Lord warn Jeremiah not to trust?

answers: Because they speak kindly to him
Because they prosper even while dealing treacherously
medium.explanation: Jeremiah questions why treacherous and wicked people are allowed to prosper.
medium.q: Why does Jeremiah ask for the wicked to be judged?

answers: He will face even greater difficulties
medium.explanation: The comparison between running with footmen and contending with horses points to greater trials ahead.
medium.q: What does the Lord's answer suggest about Jeremiah's future difficulties?

answers: Far from their inward thoughts and hearts
medium.explanation: The wicked speak of God with their mouths, but He is far from their inner thoughts and affections.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “far from their reins” mean in context?

answers: They are near in their mouths but far from their inner selves
They are weak in body but strong in spirit
They are poor but honor the Lord
challenge.explanation: They speak as if God is near, while their inward thoughts remain far from Him.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast in the description of the wicked?

answers: Jeremiah asks for rest, and the Lord promises it
Jeremiah complains about the wicked's prosperity, and the Lord prepares him for harder trials
Jeremiah asks for new relatives, and the Lord sends them
challenge.explanation: The Lord responds not only to the wicked's prosperity but also to Jeremiah's need for endurance.
challenge.q: How does Jeremiah's complaint relate to the Lord's response?

answers: Kind words do not prove faithfulness
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah's relatives betrayed him despite speaking fair words, so actions must be considered as well as words.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the warning not to believe relatives who speak fair words?

paragraphs.title: The Abandonment of the Inheritance and Its Desolation

answers: He moved them into the wilderness
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I have forsaken mine house, I have left mine heritage.”
easy.q: What did the Lord do to His house and inheritance?

easy.explanation: The shepherds destroyed the vineyard and made the pleasant portion a desolate wilderness.
easy.q: What did the pleasant portion become?

answers: They sowed wheat but reaped thorns
They sowed thorns but reaped wheat
easy.explanation: The passage says, “They have sown wheat, but shall reap thorns.”
easy.q: What happened to the wheat that was sown?

answers: Shepherds, spoilers, and wild creatures ruined it
Only a lack of rain harmed it
The people built too many cities there
medium.explanation: Pastors destroyed the vineyard, spoilers came upon the land, and beasts were called to devour it.
medium.q: Why is the inheritance described as having suffered many attacks?

medium.explanation: The KJV says, “No flesh shall have peace.”
medium.q: What was one result of the destruction of the land?

medium.explanation: The word describes land that has been ruined, abandoned, and made empty.
medium.q: What does “desolate” mean in this passage?

answers: The ruin of the inheritance leads to desolation and disappointing crops
Desolation leads to prosperity and peace
The absence of enemies leads to destruction
challenge.explanation: The attacks on the land result in desolation, lack of peace, and a failed harvest.
challenge.q: What cause-and-effect relationship appears in these verses?

answers: It has become wild and hostile
challenge.explanation: The inheritance cries out like a lion, presenting an image of something fierce and hostile.
challenge.q: What does the image of the inheritance as a lion communicate?

answers: No one takes the destruction seriously
Everyone understands the situation and acts
The land is filled with joyful people
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes the people's failure to consider or respond to the devastation.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the statement “no man layeth it to heart”?

paragraphs.title: Judgment on the Neighboring Nations and God's Compassion

easy.explanation: The Lord speaks against the evil neighbours who touched the inheritance of His people.
easy.q: Who would the Lord pluck out of their land?

answers: Pluck it out from among the nations
easy.explanation: The Lord says He will “pluck out the house of Judah from among them.”
easy.q: What would the Lord do to the house of Judah?

easy.explanation: The Lord promises, “I will return, and have compassion on them.”
easy.q: What would the Lord do after plucking them out?

answers: They touched the inheritance given to Israel
medium.explanation: They were judged because they harmed the inheritance that the Lord caused Israel to inherit.
medium.q: Why were the neighboring nations judged?

answers: Judgment and removal, followed by compassion and restoration
Restoration followed by removal without judgment
medium.explanation: The Lord first announces removal and then promises to return, show compassion, and restore.
medium.q: What is the order of events in these verses?

medium.explanation: Here, “heritage” refers to the land and possession given to God's people.
medium.q: What does “heritage” mean in this context?

answers: Judgment is always the final word
Restoration and compassion may follow judgment
challenge.explanation: The passage presents both removal and a later promise of compassion and restoration.
challenge.q: What does the movement from judgment to compassion reveal about the Lord's actions?

answers: Those who were removed, brought back to their heritage and land
challenge.explanation: The Lord promises to bring them again, every man to his heritage and land.
challenge.q: Who is included in the promised restoration?

answers: The nations' attack on the inheritance is the reason for their judgment
The inheritance has no connection to the judgment
The inheritance is only where the shepherds are sent
challenge.explanation: The neighboring nations are judged because they touched the inheritance given to God's people.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the inheritance and the judgment?

paragraphs.title: The Possibility of Restoration or Destruction

easy.explanation: The Lord says they must diligently learn the ways of His people.
easy.q: What must the neighboring nations learn in order to be built among God's people?

easy.explanation: They must swear, “The Lord liveth,” rather than swear by Baal.
easy.q: By whose name must they swear?

answers: They will be built among God's people
They will be plucked up and destroyed
easy.explanation: The Lord says He will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation if it will not obey.
easy.q: What will happen if they will not obey?

answers: They must learn God's ways and swear by His name
They must produce a great harvest
They must build vineyards in the wilderness
medium.explanation: Learning God's ways and swearing by His name are presented as the conditions for being built among His people.
medium.q: What is the condition for the nations to be restored among God's people?

answers: Being built among God's people versus being plucked up and destroyed
medium.explanation: Obedience leads to being built among God's people, while disobedience leads to destruction.
medium.q: What contrast is presented in these verses?

answers: They will be established and included among God's people
They will be planted in fields
medium.explanation: In context, being built means being established and included within God's people.
medium.q: What does “they shall be built in the midst of my people” mean?

answers: They must replace allegiance to Baal with allegiance to the Lord
It does not matter whose name they use
Baal and the Lord are presented as the same deity
challenge.explanation: The passage requires them to abandon the former practice of swearing by Baal and swear by the Lord instead.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the contrast between swearing by the Lord and swearing by Baal?

answers: They remove every possibility of change
They present an opportunity for correction alongside a warning of punishment
challenge.explanation: Alongside the threat of destruction, the Lord offers restoration to those who learn and obey His ways.
challenge.q: How do these verses continue the theme of judgment in the preceding verses?

answers: Restoration depends on the nations' behavior
The nations have already been built among God's people
challenge.explanation: The word “if” shows that restoration is conditional upon learning God's ways and obeying Him.
challenge.q: What does the word “if” show about the first possible outcome?
